name: call_routine_with_span_length
description: Reads a first field and two 16-bit fields from the parameter block, computes an inclusive span length as the difference between the two fields plus one, and passes the first field, the start field and that length to one routine.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:2:1F26

description: Calls one routine to fill a local buffer, runs two counting loops with empty bodies, makes several calls, and adds a value at a fixed offset from the base register, a local byte and a call result. The sum is stored through the pointer argument when it is non-null and is also returned.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:2:1F2C
name: convert_value_to_word
description: Returns zero when its argument is zero. Otherwise it passes the argument to one routine, then passes that routine's result and the address of a local 16-bit output to a second routine, and returns the value written there.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:2:1F32
name: configure_state_by_mode
description: Copies six entries from a fixed table into a local, repeatedly calls one routine and another until the first returns zero, and copies a few words into a state block. It then branches on a mode argument, and each mode writes its own set of state fields and makes a few calls with fixed reference values.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:2:1F38
name: wait_for_flag_and_lookup
description: Busy-waits until a flag byte in the state block is nonzero, copies that flag, clears it, and returns the entry of a byte table at the index given by the flag value, widened to 16 bits.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:2:1F3E
name: store_mode_flags_from_state
description: Copies two words from fixed memory locations into the state block, sets a boolean word to one when a stored state word equals one, and stores two in a byte when that state word equals two and zero otherwise.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:2:1F44
name: return_absolute_word_value
description: Returns the absolute value of its argument, truncated to 16 bits, by negating it when it is below zero.

name: change_stored_selection
description: Compares a 16-bit argument with a stored selection word and, when they differ, releases the previous selection if one was set. For a nonzero new selection it reads a 32-bit entry from a table indexed by the selection, calls routines with a fixed constant and a stored long, and then records the new selection.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:2:1F62
name: store_pair_into_pointer_list
description: Copies the two 32-bit words of its argument block into every non-null destination pointer in the trailing stack argument list, stopping at the first null entry, and returns zero.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:2:1F68
name: call_routine_with_row_address
description: Takes a 32-bit value, uses its upper 16 bits times 64 plus a fixed base offset as an address, passes that address to one routine, then calls a second routine with no arguments.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:2:1F6E
name: adjust_offset_and_pass_on
description: Calls one routine, subtracts a stored word from the value pointed to by its argument, adds 3600 when a stored flag is nonzero, and passes the address of the result to another routine.

name: clear_bit_when_flag_set
description: Returns zero unless a global flag byte is nonzero. When the flag is set, it clears the lowest bit of a fixed memory byte, sets a result to zero, calls one routine, and returns that call's result.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:9:005E
name: refresh_state_from_record
description: Calls one routine, then when a global flag is set and a record pointer is nonzero it clears the low bit of a fixed byte and copies a state byte from the record into the global flag. It sets bit one of that flag when a record bit is clear and clears it when the record bit is set, stores a byte from the record and a constant, saves the record pointer, calls one routine, and sets bit zero of the output byte.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:13:0000
name: call_routine_per_string_char
description: Walks a null-terminated byte string and calls the routine passed as its first argument once for each character, stopping at the terminator. It is called by one unnamed routine.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:13:0036
name: expand_text_format_codes
description: Walks a text string and sends each ordinary character to a callback routine. A percent sign starts an escape: codes B, F, X and Y store argument values into fields of a state record, code P calls a routine with a record field, codes D, U, d and u build a value and emit it through two calls, code s emits a string argument, code c invokes the callback with no text, and any other code invokes the callback once.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:13:003A
name: expand_text_format_codes
description: Same text escape walker as its neighbouring routine: it sends ordinary characters to a callback and handles percent-sign codes that store argument values into a state record, emit strings or values, or invoke the callback. It is called by two unnamed routines.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:demo:13:02A8
name: handle_newline_or_emit_char
description: Treats a carriage return and a line feed by making one call each. For any other byte it fetches a table entry, records the byte and a width value in state, calls one routine repeatedly while a bound check against a stored limit holds, and then calls one routine once more.

name: run_callback_and_return_status

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:intro:0:0000
name: open_graphics_library_entry
description: Program entry point. It opens the graphics library by name through the system library table and keeps the returned base, sets several fixed words, calls routines, and waits in a loop on a counter. It makes one more library call, clears its state and returns.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:intro:0:00A4
name: wait_for_fire_button_release
description: Clears the sprite zero pointer and the scroll control word, then loops while polling a counter and a fire-button byte, calling three routines each pass until the button bit clears. Afterwards it calls one routine, copies a value from a library-returned structure, and clears its state.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:intro:0:0AE4
name: program_blitter_and_expand_bits
description: Waits for a status flag, then programs the blitter's control, mask, pointer and size registers. It then runs an eight-step loop that shifts a 16-bit word one bit at a time, writing eight table entries for each set bit and clearing them for each clear bit.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:intro:0:0AEE
name: program_blitter_and_expand_bits
description: Programs the blitter with the same register sequence and bit-expansion loop as its neighbouring routine, but without returning a value from its final library call.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:intro:0:0AFE
name: program_blitter_and_expand_bits
description: Programs the blitter with the same register sequence and bit-expansion loop as its neighbouring routines, calling four unnamed routines and returning nothing.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:intro:0:0C34
name: read_next_offset_byte
description: Reads the next byte at a cursor, wrapping the cursor back to the start of a buffer when it reaches a sentinel value of minus one. It stores the byte, offset by the letter J, into a global and advances the cursor.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:intro:0:0C92
name: call_handler_then_set_bit
description: Calls the routine stored at a fixed pointer, then sets bit one of a global flag byte.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:intro:0:0CA2
name: call_indirect_handler
description: Calls a routine through a function pointer stored at a fixed location plus an offset, with no arguments.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:intro:0:0CAC
name: reset_audio_channels_dma
description: Zeroes four audio-related registers, writes fifteen to a DMA control location and then clears bit one of it. The register list includes the four audio period registers and the DMA control register.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:intro:0:0CDA
name: build_four_entry_table
description: Sets four base pointers into a table, clears a block of 32 longs, and loops four times writing structure entries whose pointers and constants come from base offsets and a lookup. It finishes by storing a fixed control value and a flag word.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:intro:0:0DB6
name: install_handler_once
description: On its first use it saves the current global value, points the global at a routine and sets a one-time flag. Every call then clears two counters and copies a long from a table entry.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:intro:0:0E18
name: step_channel_sequence_counters
description: Calls one routine four times, storing channel selector values of 1, 2, 8 and 4 before each call. It then advances a counter that wraps at a limit read from a table, and when that counter returns to zero it advances a second counter, wraps it at its own limit and sets a flag.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:intro:0:0F0A
name: stub_empty_return
description: A routine with no body beyond return, so calling it does nothing.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:intro:0:0F10
name: step_sequence_record_state
description: A large routine with 477 instructions whose pseudo-code is truncated in the bundle. The visible part walks records in a table, reads counters and pointers from them and updates their state fields, and the register list includes the DMA control register.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:intro:0:1530
name: advance_four_audio_channel_states
description: Advances a state byte for each of four channels through a one, two, three sequence. When a channel reaches its second state, it loads a location and length from a table entry, or a stop value when the entry is the sentinel, and writes them to the audio channel location and length registers.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:intro:0:16AE
name: negate_table_entry_at_index
description: Negates one byte of a table, at an index computed from a state word plus a fixed base offset. It does nothing else.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:intro:0:16C0
name: blend_two_row_pairs
description: When each of two counters is nonzero, it fills a 32-entry destination row with the midpoint of two source rows, using signed byte values offset by 128 before averaging and then restored. Each block advances its own row index, decrements its counter, and uses a separate set of rows.

key: ultima vi - the false prophet (demo) (1992)(mindscape)[h trsi]/Ultima VI - The False Prophet (demo) (1992)(Mindscape)[h TRSi].adf:intro:0:73A0

name: stub_empty_return
description: A routine in a runtime segment that does nothing but return.

name: stub_empty_return
description: A routine in a runtime segment that does nothing but return.

name: copy_table_then_call_pointer
description: If its output pointer is non-null, copies sixteen 32-bit entries from a fixed table into that buffer. It then calls through a register-held function pointer, which the call data resolves to find_max_and_prepare_buffer.

name: find_max_entry_and_setup
description: Program entry point. It walks a linked list of nodes to find the largest value in a field, then makes library calls and, if one returns nonzero, writes that maximum and a stepping array of values into a block with a stack record holding a sentinel and pointer fields. It returns zero on success and minus one when a required call returns zero.

name: copy_table_then_call_pointer
description: If its output pointer is non-null, copies sixteen 32-bit entries from a fixed table into that buffer. It then calls through a register-held function pointer, which the call data resolves to find_max_and_prepare_buffer.

name: parse_command_line_and_run
description: Program entry point. It allocates a control block and returns twenty if that fails. Started from Workbench it waits for and reads the startup message, otherwise it splits the command line into quoted or space-separated arguments, converts star-N and star-E escapes to newline and escape characters, and stores pointers to them in the block. It opens the dos and related libraries through library bases and, on exit, frees the block and closes them.

name: store_and_release_state_slot
description: Looks up the current task's state block, stores its parameter in the state slot, then conditionally calls cleanup routines from fields of that record and makes one more call. It returns the stored parameter.

name: run_icon_program_with_buffer
description: Sets up options from its parameter block and looks up a window or icon handler, then allocates a 1536-byte buffer and fills it through a loop of helper calls before passing it to a processing routine. If the allocation fails it copies a message and calls one routine with the value 200 instead.

name: handle_icon_request_result
description: Clears a byte in the buffer and runs a lookup on the request, reading its first character. For a single dot it makes further handler calls and updates the buffer, otherwise it calls a handler with the response, then conditionally calls one routine with a fixed value based on a flag and the result.

name: initialise_library_and_functions
description: When its parameter pointer is non-null, it makes a library from the record's first field, creates its functions from a second field, and enables them. It returns the result of the final call.

name: join_path_nodes_with_colon
description: Allocates a 260-byte scratch buffer, then walks a linked list of text nodes and appends each node's string with a separator, skipping short entries. It replaces the first slash in the result with a colon when one exists, otherwise it appends a fixed text that the bundle identifies as RAM:, then frees the scratch buffer.

name: chain_calls_with_offset
description: Makes two calls that pass its three arguments through, uses the result of a third call on its second and third arguments to compute an offset from the first, and calls one routine with that offset.

name: count_string_length
description: Returns the number of bytes before the terminating zero of a string passed by pointer. It walks the string one byte at a time, incrementing a counter until it reaches the zero byte.

name: copy_null_terminated_string
description: Copies bytes from a source string into a destination buffer, including the terminating zero byte.

name: skip_string_end_and_call
description: Advances a pointer to the terminating zero of a string, then calls one routine with that position and the second argument unchanged.

name: parse_signed_decimal
description: Reads an optional leading plus or minus sign and then the decimal digits of a number, stopping at the first non-digit, and returns the signed value.

name: call_with_stack_slot_pointer
description: Calls one routine with its two arguments and the address of its stack-argument area, then returns.

name: format_buffer_and_measure
description: Calls a library routine through a global table entry, which the facts identify as a text formatting call, into a 140-byte stack buffer. It then counts the characters up to the terminating zero and, when the count is nonzero, passes the buffer and its count to one routine.

name: call_format_library_entry
description: Calls the library routine stored at a fixed offset in a global table, which the facts identify as a text formatting call, then returns.

name: store_byte_at_output_pointer
description: Stores the low byte of the data register through the address register pointer, without moving the pointer. Another routine takes its address, so it probably serves as a single-byte output callback.

name: load_hunk_file_with_relocation
description: Program entry for loading an AmigaDOS executable. It reads hunk type codes, allocates memory for each hunk through a library call, copies data hunks and gives BSS hunks no data, then applies 32-bit relocation entries by adding the load base to each listed longword until the end marker.

name: delay_loop_count_down
description: Busy-waits by decrementing a 16-bit count register until it wraps past zero.

name: unpack_compressed_stream_backwards
description: Unpacks a compressed stream into a buffer from its end toward its start. It reads bit codes through helper routines and either writes literal bytes or copies a run of earlier bytes, using run lengths and distances from a code table, and it stops when the output pointer reaches the buffer start.

name: shift_bit_buffer_by_count
description: Shifts a bit buffer held in two registers one bit per step, for a count given in a 16-bit register. When the buffer empties it loads the next word from memory, and it leaves the bit that is shifted out for the caller to read.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiler reports bad instruction data after a trap instruction and truncates the block, so no behaviour is recovered.

name: scan_bit_masks_and_count
description: Program entry point whose pseudo-code is truncated in the bundle. The visible part writes a one- or two-digit number into a text buffer, initialises a table of minus-one entries, and scans bit masks over a block, comparing bit values, counting changes and calling library routines.

name: run_forever_main_loop
description: Program entry point that stores a few fixed addresses, calls five routines in sequence, then loops forever calling two routines. It never returns.

name: stub_empty_return
description: A routine that does nothing but return.

name: init_table_entries_with_delay
description: Fills groups of table entries with fixed words, then busy-waits through a nested counting loop. If a flag global is nonzero, it writes two fixed words to several locations and adds a scaled value to a series of table entries.

name: split_base_into_pointers
description: Reads a 32-bit base address from a fixed structure and writes its high and low 16-bit halves into several pointer locations. Four consecutive pointers are offset from the base by multiples of 8000.

name: copy_table_and_combine_rows
description: Copies 480 longs from one table to another, then runs four groups in which words from three source rows are combined by bitwise operations into a destination row. Each result is split into high and low halves, and each group ends with two zero words.

name: process_audio_channel_requests
description: Checks four per-channel request bits in a state word. For each requested channel whose busy bit is clear, it marks the channel busy and stores a channel selector of one, two, four or eight with the request bit. The register list includes the audio volume, DMA control and interrupt registers.

name: start_audio_channel_playback
description: Starts playback on a free audio channel by choosing an entry whose state is not six, then storing its sample pointer, length and period fields. It returns early when a channel is already in one of its active states.

name: load_ready_channels_into_hardware
description: For each of four channel blocks that is marked active and matches a sequence value, copies its pointer, length and period into the channel's hardware registers. It then sets the DMA and interrupt enable bits and clears the block's active flag.

name: open_and_read_file_retrying
description: Opens a file through the dos library, repeating the open while it returns zero, then repeats the read while it reports an error. It closes the file and the library, and returns its original argument, or a failure marker when the first library call fails.

name: close_dos_file_and_library
description: Closes a file through the dos library, then closes the library base and returns its stored argument.

name: write_file_or_fail
description: Opens a file and writes through the dos library. On success it closes the file and the library and returns its argument; otherwise it reads the dos error code, closes both, and returns a failure marker.

name: open_dos_library_base
description: Opens the dos library by name through the exec library and stores its base in a global variable.

name: close_after_io_error
description: Fetches the dos error code, closes the file and the dos library, and returns a failure marker.

name: open_and_record_handle
description: Opens a file and, when the open succeeds, calls one more library routine and stores its low-word result in a global. A failure at either step closes the file and library before returning.

name: decode_keyboard_scancode
description: Reads and clears a pending keyboard byte, inverts it, and decodes it to a character through a table of printable keys from the first keyboard row. Two key codes reset a state flag instead.

name: clear_flag_on_key_codes
description: Clears a global flag when the low seven bits of its argument are 96 or 97, and returns the argument unchanged otherwise.

name: install_hook_and_enable_interrupts
description: Opens the graphics library, saves one of its fields and replaces it with a pointer, then writes interrupt control values and a handler address to hardware. It closes the library before returning.

name: restore_dma_and_interrupt_state
description: Calls one routine, then writes fixed control values to the DMA and interrupt registers, writes two saved values back, and finally sets interrupt enable bits with a fixed mask.

name: service_interrupt_request_bits
description: Checks interrupt request bits. When one bit is set it stores a fixed code and clears the status. When another is set and a pointer differs from its sentinel, it queues a routine result into a 32-entry ring buffer, increments a counter, and recomputes two status bytes.

name: queue_button_event_when_set
description: Handles a button-state input passed in a register. When one bit is set and a pointer differs from its sentinel, it queues a routine result into a 32-entry ring buffer, increments a counter, and recomputes two status bytes.

name: update_clamped_position_counters
description: Updates two position counters from the change in a global input since the last call. Each change is limited to a range of plus or minus 255, the results are clamped to fixed ranges, and one counter is raised to a minimum read from a table.

name: update_clamped_position_counters
description: Performs the same clamped position update as its neighbouring routine, reached from another caller. It updates two counters from the change in a global input and clamps them to fixed ranges.

name: apply_clamped_position_delta
description: Adds a signed step computed from two register inputs to one position counter and clamps the result to a fixed range. It then applies the same minimum and maximum clamps to the second counter as its neighbours.

name: update_position_from_mouse_port
description: Clamps one position counter, updates the second from the change in a value read from the mouse movement register, clamps it to a fixed range, and applies the minimum from a table.

name: set_clamped_position_from_inputs
description: Sets one position counter from a register input plus a signed step, clamps it to a fixed range, and applies the same minimum from a table and maximum clamps as its neighbours.

name: clamp_position_counters
description: Clamps the position counters to their fixed ranges, raising one to a table minimum and capping the other, with no other changes.

name: forbid_task_switching
description: Calls the exec library's Forbid routine to stop task switching, then returns its input registers unchanged.

name: swap_pointers_then_wait
description: Disables one interrupt, swaps two saved longs in a structure, and sets a flag word to one. It then waits until the interrupt request bit is set, calls one routine, and writes the interrupt enable value again.

name: wait_for_interrupt_then_enable
description: Busy-waits until the interrupt request bit is set, then writes the interrupt enable value for that interrupt.

name: match_text_and_parse_fields
description: Compares a block of 16 characters at a fixed location with the text at a stored pointer. On a full match it parses several digit fields into state variables and advances the pointer; otherwise it calls one library routine, then a reset routine and a fixed low address that is not a meaningful routine.

name: match_text_and_parse_fields
description: Compares a block of 16 characters at a fixed location with the text at a stored pointer. On a full match it parses several digit fields into state variables and advances the pointer; otherwise it calls one library routine, then a reset routine and a fixed low address that is not a meaningful routine.

name: match_text_and_parse_fields
description: Same text matching routine as its neighbours, reached from a different caller. On a full match it parses the same digit fields into state variables; otherwise it takes the same library and reset path.

name: match_text_and_parse_fields
description: Same text matching routine as its neighbours, reached from a different caller. On a full match it parses the same digit fields into state variables; otherwise it takes the same library and reset path.

name: match_text_and_parse_fields
description: Same text matching and field parsing routine as its neighbours, reached from a different caller.

name: dispatch_queued_handler
description: When a queue index differs from the write index, it takes the next queued handler from a 32-entry table and advances the index with wrap at 32. If a flag is clear and that handler code is 97, it runs the reset path.

name: store_argument_in_state_field
description: Stores its stack argument into a fixed field of the state block. The facts list a Supervisor library call elsewhere, but this routine performs only the store.

name: reset_then_invalid_call
description: Calls a reset routine and then calls a fixed low address, which is not a valid routine, so the routine likely reaches an invalid target. No further behaviour is recovered.

name: program_blitter_from_state
description: Waits for the blitter to finish, then programs its mask, modulo, pointer, control and size registers from positions in a state record and a table, and starts the operation through the size register.

name: reprogram_blitter_from_saved_pointer
description: Waits for the blitter to finish, then reprograms its mask, control, modulo and pointer registers from a saved pointer in the state record, and starts the size register.

name: compose_entry_list_and_text
description: Copies table values into state fields, computes a total from fixed multipliers and delay counts, and builds a list of entries from a second table. When a text buffer pointer is set it writes a three-digit value as characters and waits for 50 calls; otherwise it waits for 250 calls and takes the reset path.

name: decompress_lzss_stream
description: Decompresses a stream in the classic LZSS style. It fills a 4096-byte ring buffer with spaces, then reads flag bits, copying literal bytes or repeating earlier bytes from the ring through a 12-bit offset and a length of at least two, and stops when the output count reaches zero.

name: scan_records_and_update_state
description: Large routine with 212 instructions whose pseudo-code is truncated in the bundle. The visible part walks a table of 12-byte records to find one matching a stored value, updates counter and pointer fields, and calls routines to process the matched entry, returning early in some cases.

name: format_three_digit_number_text
description: Writes a 16-bit number as three decimal digit characters into a buffer. Leading zero digits are replaced by spaces, and the units digit is always kept as a digit.

name: split_pixels_into_four_arrays
description: Looks up each masked value of 20 rows of 16 entries in a table, combines it with a fixed mask, and writes one byte to each of four byte arrays spaced 8000 bytes apart.

name: update_entry_flags_next
description: Sets a flag bit on list entries that match a current index and clears it on the others, then selects the next item from a pointer list and updates a row byte from a table. Finally it clears two flag bytes for entries whose fields have changed.

name: advance_countdown_table_entry
description: When a countdown counter expires, it reads the next entry from a table, stores an index, and calls routines to step through the data. Other countdown counters select alternative paths, and the pseudo-code is truncated after the first set of paths.

name: select_entry_and_wait_timer
description: Selects an entry by index, records it in the state, and loads its pointer and count fields from tables. It then loops waiting for a timer value and calling routines on each pass until the table entry ends. The referenced text includes a FAILED message, and the pseudo-code shown covers only the selection loop.

name: select_entry_and_wait_timer
description: Same table-driven entry selection and timer loop as its neighbour, without the first check against the current index.

name: combine_digit_string_with_table
description: Combines an eight-character decimal digit string with eight table bytes, working from the first digit onward and carrying between digits. Each result is written back as a digit character after a complement step.

name: subtract_digit_string_with_table
description: Subtracts eight table bytes from an eight-character decimal digit string, working from the first digit onward with a borrow between digits. Each result is complemented before the subtraction and written back as a digit character.

name: subtract_digit_string_with_table
description: Same complement and subtract digit routine as its neighbour, reached from another caller.

name: step_timed_entries_until_end
description: Repeatedly waits for a timer value to reach a stored time, advances that time by four, and calls two routines, until the table entry it reads is zero.

name: draw_text_glyphs_to_planes
description: Walks a null-terminated text and draws each character as eight rows of glyph bits into four byte arrays spaced 8000 bytes apart, using a font table indexed by character code. A space fills the rows with a fixed pattern instead, and a word that matches the sentinel saves the text pointer first.

name: repeat_call_eleven_times
description: Fetches the next word of a stream, saving a pointer when the word is the sentinel, then calls one routine eleven times.

name: repeat_routine_in_three_passes
description: Calls one routine seven times per pass across three passes, with no other work.

name: fill_block_after_counter
description: When one state value differs from another it advances a counter. While the counter is below three it calls one routine; after that it fills a block of bytes with 255 at a stride of 40 bytes, using a table offset.

name: fill_block_with_register_byte
description: Fills a block of bytes with the byte passed in a data register, using a table offset selected from the register value and the same stride as its neighbour.

name: initialise_display_state_and_labels
description: Initialises display state: sets 594 word pairs to zero and 65535, copies a source table of 4000 words into four arrays spaced 8000 bytes apart, copies 8192 longs back, and sets a few flags and values. It builds label text from fixed strings chosen by a state index, and the referenced text includes labels such as BEAM IN FEET and MAXIMUM SPEED.

name: pack_four_arrays_into_words
description: Copies from four 16-bit arrays spaced 8000 bytes apart into one interleaved table, writing four words per entry for 84 rows of seven entries and advancing the source 20 words per row.

name: unpack_table_into_four_arrays
description: Copies from an interleaved table of four words per entry back into four 16-bit arrays spaced 8000 bytes apart, for 84 rows of seven entries. It is the reverse of its neighbour.

name: run_display_update_loop
description: Sets up a display frame, copies arrays, and builds entry lists from tables. It then runs a loop that compares old and new values, calls routines to redraw changed items and text, and waits on a timer each pass until a counter reaches zero.

name: initialise_display_buffers_and_pattern
description: Initialises display state: copies 32 longs and a block of 4000 words into arrays, rearranges byte groups into four pattern arrays, and fills a 256-entry table with complement values. It reads a flag and sets a state value from the global data, then calls several routines.

name: draw_text_glyphs_to_planes
description: Draws each character of a null-terminated text as eight rows of glyph bits into four byte arrays, combining the glyph with a masked source word. A space writes a fixed pattern instead. It is the same routine as its neighbour, reached from another caller.

name: blend_masked_planes_into_block
description: Combines three masked source words into four byte arrays for three groups of eight rows, choosing its masks from a state value. When the state is zero it writes nothing.

name: initialise_pattern_table_and_interrupts
description: Initialises a pattern table, copies rows of data from four arrays into a working buffer, and sets position and clamp values. It zeroes a 200-entry table that steps by 40, then sets interrupt-related registers, calling routines in between.

name: update_position_from_buttons
description: Reads fire and side button bits from the button registers and sets a direction value from them. It then updates position fields from state, walks a list of entries to process the matching one, and advances a counter that wraps at ten.

name: update_position_and_entries
description: Performs the same position and entry update as its neighbour, using the stored direction value instead of reading the buttons.

name: set_entry_angle_from_table
description: Sets a field of an entry from a table indexed by a value, and negates a second field when the value is eighteen. It makes two calls and then advances a counter that wraps at ten.

name: set_entry_angle_second_table
description: Sets a field of an entry from a second table indexed by a value, and negates a second field when the value is eighteen. It makes two calls and then advances a counter that wraps at ten.

name: find_entry_and_advance_state
description: Searches a list of entries for one whose two position fields match the arguments, then updates its direction-related field from a table and calls routines. It ends by advancing a counter that wraps at ten.

name: load_table_entry_into_state
description: Looks up an 8-byte entry in a table using a field of its argument, copies the entry's two longs into state fields, and calls one routine.

name: merge_masked_rows_into_arrays
description: Loops 16 times over two sets of four arrays spaced 8000 bytes apart. It clears bits in each destination word with a mask from state, then ORs shifted source words into both sets.

name: run_forever_main_loop
description: Program entry that copies six longs from its argument block into a fixed location, stores a pointer, calls four routines, then loops forever calling four routines. It never returns.

name: init_table_entries_with_delay
description: Fills six groups of table entries with fixed words, busy-waits through a nested counting loop, and if a flag global is nonzero writes fixed words to several locations and adds a scaled value to two series of table entries. It then sets offset variants of a value across a 12-entry table.

name: copy_twelve_words_from_row
description: Copies twelve words from a row of a table, selected by a state field divided by four, into a destination with a stride of six words.
